subject: maths
question: Anil sold an article at a loss of 15%. Had he sold it for Rs. 84 more, he would have gained 13%. At what price should he have sold if to gain 20% ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total difference in percentage = **Gain% − (−Loss%)** = 13% + 15% = 28%

According to the question, 28% of **Cost Price (CP)** = ₹84

Then, 1% of CP = 84 ÷ 28 = ₹3

To gain **20% profit**, required **Selling Price (SP)** = 120% of CP

Required SP = 120 × 3 = ₹360

**∴ The correct answer is ₹360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **Loss** = 15%, Hypothetical **Gain** = 13%, Difference in SP = ₹84.

**Formula Used:** Selling Price = CP × (100 ± Profit or Loss%)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/780cbe0435025621a4d2cb6aae2ec1b02371d54a50c91938160626cf5a95818a.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article be 100 units.

⇒ Case 1: 15% Loss → SP₁ = 100 − 15 = 85 units.

⇒ Case 2: 13% Gain → SP₂ = 100 + 13 = 113 units.

⇒ Difference = SP₂ − SP₁ = 113 − 85 = 28 units.

⇒ 28 units = ₹84

⇒ 1 unit = 84 ÷ 28 = ₹3

⇒ CP = 100 units = 100 × 3 = ₹300

⇒ Required SP for 20% gain = 300 × (120/100) = 300 × 1.2

⇒ Required SP = ₹360

**∴ The correct answer is ₹360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss on Cost Price

Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise. Profit = SP − CP, Loss = CP − SP.

Combined Percentage Change

When there is a shift from a **Loss** to a **Profit**, the total percentage change is the numerical sum of the two percentages: Total % Change = Profit% + Loss%.

Marked Price and Discount

**Marked Price (MP)** is the price printed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on MP: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100.
